entrypoints.summary: The report describes KyberSlash1 timing observations during Kyber decapsulation using attacker-selected ciphertexts.
The supplied demo implements the attacker, decapsulation target, timing collection, and recovered-key comparison.

affected_components.role: Converts polynomial coefficients to a 32-byte message; its prior quantization expression contained the division.

causal_paths.kind: secret-derived coefficient quantization to timing oracle

code_slices.fixed: The patch changes t to uint32_t and computes the quantization as left shift, add 1665, multiply 80635, right shift 28, then mask one bit.
code_slices.surrounding_context: poly_tomsg iterates over KYBER_N/8 output bytes and eight coefficients per byte, placing each resulting bit into msg[i].
code_slices.vulnerable: The pre-patch poly_tomsg obtains t from a polynomial coefficient, conditionally normalizes it, then calculates a one-bit quantization using ((t << 1) + KYBER_Q/2) / KYBER_Q.

observability.channel: decapsulation timing and local recovered-key comparison
negative_controls: The supplied materials contain no recorded execution result for a fixed build.
The report cautions that sufficient noise, or ciphertext-dependent noise, can make the demo fail.
observability.positive_marker: A guessed secret key recomputes to the public key and the demo judge prints that every recovered coefficient matches.

preconditions: A target performs repeated Kyber decapsulations under the same secret key.
The target build exhibits the documented variable-time division behavior; the demonstrated scope is the pinned reference revision on Raspbian gcc 8.3.0 and Raspberry Pi 2.
The attacker can obtain sufficiently stable decapsulation timing observations for selected ciphertexts.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: The demo uses seven selected ciphertext choices for each of 512 secret positions and repeats each ciphertext 16 times per batch.
trigger_steps.summary: Build and run the public demo against its pinned vulnerable pq-crystals/kyber revision with KYBER_K=2 on Raspberry Pi 2.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Repeated selected Kyber ciphertext pairs (u,v) supplied to decapsulation.
trigger_steps.summary: Aggregate timing observations, compare them against division-timing models, and validate guessed key material.

capabilities.concept: secret-key coefficient inference from decapsulation timings

mitigations.concept: multiply-and-shift message quantization that removes division

relation_candidates.rationale: Selected ciphertexts drive repeated decapsulations whose timing is observed in the KyberSlash1 procedure.
The division-based quantization of a secret-derived coefficient is the documented operation whose compiled DIV behavior creates the timing signal.

relation_candidates.dst: secret-key coefficient inference from decapsulation timings
relation_candidates.rationale: The report describes comparing observed timings to division-timing models to select coefficient guesses.
The report describes complete-key reconstruction validation, and the demo checks every recovered coefficient against the target key.
relation_candidates.src: secret-key coefficient inference from decapsulation timings

relation_candidates.dst: multiply-and-shift message quantization that removes division
relation_candidates.rationale: The upstream change replaces the division-based poly_tomsg expression specifically to prevent compiler use of DIV.

impact.affected_asset: Kyber KEM recipient secret key and the confidentiality boundary it protects.
impact.attacker_capability: Obtain repeated decapsulation timing observations for selected ciphertexts and infer secret-key coefficients from the timing signal.
impact.security_effect: Timing side channel enabling recovery of a Kyber recipient's complete reusable secret key on the demonstrated platform and toolchain.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker submits selected ciphertexts to repeated decapsulation operations under a reusable Kyber secret key.

A secret-derived polynomial coefficient is quantized in poly_tomsg through a C division expression; on the demonstrated build, compilation exposes a variable-time division operation instead of preserving constant-time handling of that value.
The prior poly_tomsg expression computes ((t << 1) + KYBER_Q/2) / KYBER_Q and masks its result; the upstream commit identifies this site as needing change to prevent compiler use of DIV.

Repeated timing observations are compared with division-timing models to guess secret coefficients; the report's demo procedure recomputes the public key from a guess and stops on a match, and the demo code separately compares recovered and target secret-key coefficients.

failure.operation: Division-based poly_tomsg quantization of a secret-derived coefficient

primary_invariant.statement: The message-decoding quantization in poly_tomsg must not execute an input-variable-time operation on a value derived from a secret polynomial coefficient.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The vulnerable source division by KYBER_Q gave the compiler an opportunity to generate DIV; the documented demonstrated build leaked timing that varied with the secret-derived division input.

quality.review_notes: Primary report, public demo, upstream diff, and patched source were inspected. The exploit evidence is explicitly scoped to the demo-pinned reference revision, Raspbian/gcc 8.3.0, and Raspberry Pi 2; it must not be generalized to all Kyber versions, compilers, or processors. The demo and report define an oracle and procedure but the bundle contains no captured successful execution output, so no run is claimed.

remediation.invariant_restored: At this poly_tomsg operation, the division expression is replaced with shift, addition, multiplication by 80635, right shift by 28, and a one-bit mask, removing the documented compiler DIV opportunity.
mitigation_classes: replace compiler-DIV-generating secret arithmetic with bounded reciprocal-style multiply-and-shift quantization
review generated code and constant-time behavior for secret-derived operations

affected_versions_or_commits.value: Raspbian with gcc 8.3.0 on Raspberry Pi 2, as demonstrated

oracle.channel: local timing measurements plus reconstructed-key comparison
oracle.expected_negative: After the poly_tomsg division is replaced by the patched multiply-and-shift sequence, this particular DIV-generating expression is absent from the source; no supplied artifact records a timing-attack run against the fixed build.
oracle.expected_positive: For the demo-pinned vulnerable revision on the specified Raspberry Pi 2 environment, collected decapsulation timings permit a secret-key guess whose recomputed public key matches; the demo judge reports all recovered coefficients equal to Bob's.
